popCulture.title: Iliad
popCulture.creator: Homer
popCulture.description: Aeneas recounts his pedigree to Achilles: Capys son of Assaracus and father of Anchises — the Dardanian link Homer fixes between Tros and the Trojan hero.

popCulture.title: Capys (son of Assaracus)
popCulture.description: Dardanian king, father of Anchises — not Capys of Alba Longa, nor every later Capys who shares the name in Italian foundation myth.

popCulture.title: Anchises
popCulture.description: Capys' son — Aphrodite's beloved and Aeneas' father, the next step of the Dardanid line Capys holds.

popCulture.title: Assaracus
popCulture.description: Capys' father — the Dardanian brother of Ilus through whom the quieter Trojan stem descends.
